stories.text: Global technology shares fall sharply, as investors worry that the US midterm results could bring tougher scrutiny of data centres and the AI industry.
Metropolitan Police chief Sir Mark Rowley will warn that policing is heading for failure without reform, saying it cannot cope with sophisticated modern criminals.
Police say Russell Brand is being investigated over two new rape complaints, and hope the guilty verdicts will encourage other potential victims.
Employers are told to include salaries in job adverts before a new law, with the government saying it will help jobseekers and curb pay discrimination.
The governor of California commutes the sentences of all 548 people on the state's death row, historically the largest in the US.
Labour is weakening Margaret Thatcher's Right to Buy housing policy, raising questions over whether the change will fix Britain's social housing problems.
The White House denies that Hegseth and Rubio will leave their posts after Republican election losses, amid calls to replace Hegseth, who faces possible impeachment.
Trump signs an order to stop future presidents altering the Oval Office, after his major changes to its decor and demolition of the East Wing.
A police car is set on fire in Glasgow as Bonfire Night disorder in Scotland leads to seven arrests and fireworks thrown at emergency workers.
A Palace aide says the King relishes politically charged trips, after facing questions over UK involvement in the slave trade during his Caribbean tour.
